summary.name: Observability: the new wave or buzzword?
summary.one_liner: A 2017 essay arguing that "observability" is a new umbrella term for monitoring plus debugging, driven by softer, more distributed system failures that are harder to diagnose.
keywords: monitoring in the time of cloud native
use_cases: Understanding why the term observability emerged
Explaining monitoring vs debugging to a team
Reading background for SRE and oncall practices
Deciding how to combine logs, metrics and traces
summary.what_it_does: This is an opinion essay, not a software tool. It argues that modern systems fail softly and in more ways, so alerts on a few key metrics are no longer enough. It frames monitoring as answering whether a system works and observability as answering why it is not working. It lists trends to watch: developer-focused tooling, faceting metrics by dimensions, integrating logging, metrics and tracing, and reducing duplicate instrumentation code (e.g., via OpenTracing). It mentions large-company tools such as Google's Dapper, Facebook's Canopy and Scuba, and Twitter's Finagle as early examples.
notable: Frames observability as monitoring plus debugging, with debugging as the larger part of the iceberg
Explains why microservices make failures harder to diagnose
Cites Cindy Sridharan and Baron Schwartz on the monitoring vs observability distinction
caveats: Opinion piece written in 2017-2018; tooling and references may be dated
Not a tool; it names no product that can be installed or purchased
